meta.description: Provides an interactive CICS screen for bank administrators to add, update, or delete Transaction Type reference data records in the database.
meta.process_description: COTRTUPC is the online update/maintenance program for the Transaction Type reference table, working in tandem with the list/browse program COTRTLIC. A bank administrator can search for a transaction type by its 2-character code, view its current description, and then choose to modify the description, delete the record, or create a new transaction type entry. The program enforces a multi-step confirmation workflow: changes are first validated, then presented for confirmation before being committed to the database, and deletions require an explicit F4 confirmation step to prevent accidental removal. It maintains data integrity by detecting concurrent modifications (record changed by another user) and locking records during the update process.

files.DCLTRTYP: Transaction Type reference table (DB2) — the primary table being maintained, storing 2-character transaction type codes and their 50-character descriptions
files.DCLTRCAT: Transaction Category reference table (DB2) — related reference data potentially used for validation or display context
files.COTRTUP (mapset): CICS BMS screen map definition for the Transaction Type update/maintenance screen presented to the administrator

business_rules: Transaction type codes are exactly 2 characters and must be alphanumeric — blank or invalid codes are rejected with an appropriate error message.
Transaction type descriptions are up to 50 characters; blank descriptions are not permitted for active records.
A multi-step confirmation is required for updates: changes are validated first, displayed for review, and only committed to the database after the administrator explicitly presses F5 to confirm.
Deletions require a separate explicit confirmation step (F4) to prevent accidental removal of transaction type reference data.

The program detects concurrent modification: if the record has been changed by another user between the time it was fetched and the time the update is submitted, the administrator is warned and the update is rejected.
If the database record cannot be locked for update, the operation is aborted and the administrator is notified.
No changes are committed if the administrator's input is identical to the values originally retrieved from the database (no-change detection).
The administrator can cancel an in-progress update or delete at any point, returning the system to a safe state with an appropriate cancellation message.
Navigation is controlled via PF keys: F3 exits to the admin menu, F12 cancels the current operation, and invalid PF key presses are rejected with an error message.
The program participates in the broader admin workflow, receiving context from COTRTLIC (list screen) and returning control to the admin menu (COADM01C) upon exit.

Documents that the following copied routine is responsible for recording which PF key the administrator pressed on the maintenance screen.
Closing boundary of the section header for the PF key capture utility.

Incorporates the shared PF key capture routine, which reads and stores the administrator's last key press (e.g., F3 exit, F4 confirm delete, F5 confirm update, F12 cancel) so the program can route to the correct next workflow step.
Closes the COPY statement that includes the PF key capture utility into the program.
Entry point for the unrecoverable error handling routine triggered when the maintenance program encounters a fatal condition.
Checks whether a specific failure message was already set by the code that detected the error, or if the crash was entirely unexpected.
If no specific error was identified, records a generic 'unexpected failure' message to ensure the incident is never silently lost.
Stamps this program (COTRTUPC) as the source of the failure, so support staff can immediately identify which maintenance program crashed.
Assigns the diagnostic code '9999' to signal a fatal, unclassified system error — distinguishing it from normal business validation errors.
Displays the full failure details (program name, error code, and message) on the administrator's screen, ensuring they are informed of the crash before the session ends.
Cancels any previously registered CICS error intercept handlers so that the forced termination below is not caught and suppressed by another routine.

Forces an immediate, hard termination of the CICS transaction using the '9999' abend code, ensuring the failure is logged in CICS system records for investigation and preventing any further processing that could corrupt the Transaction Type reference data.
Defines the exit label for the abnormal termination routine, serving as the structural closing boundary of the critical error handling section of the Transaction Type maintenance program.
Formally closes the ABEND error handling routine, returning control to the calling logic after any critical failure in the Transaction Type update or delete workflow has been processed.

variables.name: WS-MISC-STORAGE
variables.description: Top-level working storage container grouping all miscellaneous working variables used during transaction type maintenance processing — covers CICS communication, input validation, state tracking, and screen output formatting.

variables.name: WS-CICS-PROCESSNG-VARS
variables.description: Group of variables used to communicate with the CICS runtime environment during transaction type maintenance — captures results of CICS service calls such as database reads, writes, and screen interactions.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: CICS response code returned after every CICS command (e.g., database read, write, delete, screen send/receive). The program inspects this code to determine whether the operation succeeded or failed — for example, detecting that a transaction type record was not found, or that a database update was rejected.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: CICS reason code providing additional detail about why a CICS command succeeded or failed. Used alongside WS-RESP-CD to diagnose specific error conditions — for example, distinguishing between a record-not-found situation and a database lock conflict when attempting to update a transaction type.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The 4-character CICS transaction identifier for the current session. Used to re-invoke this transaction type maintenance program after the administrator interacts with the screen, ensuring the correct program is resumed when the user presses a key.

variables.name: WS-UCTRANS
variables.description: Upper-cased version of the CICS transaction identifier. Used to normalize the transaction ID to uppercase before comparison or display, ensuring consistent handling regardless of how the administrator entered the transaction code.

variables.name: WS-GENERIC-EDITS
variables.description: Group of reusable input validation work areas used when checking administrator-entered data on the transaction type maintenance screen — supports validation of alphanumeric fields such as the transaction type code and description.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME
variables.description: Holds the human-readable name of the field currently being validated (e.g., 'Transaction Type Code' or 'Description'). Used to construct meaningful error messages that tell the administrator exactly which field failed validation.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-ONLY
variables.description: Temporary work area holding the field value being checked for alphanumeric validity. During transaction type maintenance, the transaction type code and description are copied here before the generic alphanumeric validation routine inspects them character by character.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-LENGTH
variables.description: Specifies how many characters of WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-ONLY should be examined during alphanumeric validation. Set to the actual length of the field being validated (e.g., 2 for the transaction type code, up to 50 for the description) so the validation routine checks exactly the right number of characters.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-ONLY-FLAGS
variables.description: Result flag set by the generic alphanumeric validation routine after checking a field. Indicates whether the administrator's input passed validation, was blank, or contained invalid characters — driving the error message displayed on the transaction type maintenance screen.

variables.name: FLG-ALPHNANUM-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the field under validation contains acceptable alphanumeric content. When true, the administrator's input for the transaction type code or description has passed the character-content check and processing can continue.

variables.name: FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the field under validation contains invalid (non-alphanumeric) characters. When true, the program rejects the administrator's input and displays an error message identifying the offending field.

variables.name: FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the field under validation was left blank by the administrator. When true, the program rejects the input because blank transaction type codes and blank descriptions are not permitted for active reference data records.

variables.name: WS-MISC-VARS
variables.description: Group of general-purpose working variables used for formatting and string manipulation during transaction type maintenance — supports displaying database error codes and building output strings for the administrator's screen.

variables.name: WS-DISP-SQLCODE
variables.description: Formatted display version of the DB2 SQL return code from the most recent database operation. When a database error occurs during transaction type add, update, or delete, this value is included in the error message shown to the administrator so the problem can be diagnosed.

variables.name: WS-STRING-MID
variables.description: Starting position pointer used when extracting a substring from a larger text value during screen output formatting — for example, when building a display message that includes part of the transaction type code or description.

variables.name: WS-STRING-LEN
variables.description: Length counter used during string construction for screen messages — tracks how many characters have been assembled into WS-STRING-OUT when building informational or error messages for the administrator.

variables.name: WS-STRING-OUT
variables.description: Output buffer holding a formatted text string assembled for display on the transaction type maintenance screen — used to construct dynamic portions of messages shown to the administrator, such as confirmation prompts or error details.

variables.name: WS-DATACHANGED-FLAG
variables.description: Tracks whether the administrator has actually changed any field values compared to what was originally retrieved from the database. Prevents a pointless database update when the administrator submits the screen without modifying anything — enforcing the business rule that no-change submissions are rejected with an appropriate message.

variables.name: NO-CHANGES-FOUND
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator's submitted values are identical to the original database values. When true, the update workflow is halted and the administrator is informed that no changes were detected, preventing unnecessary database writes.

variables.name: CHANGE-HAS-OCCURRED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator has modified at least one field (transaction type code or description) compared to the original database record. When true, the update workflow proceeds to the confirmation step before committing changes.

variables.name: WS-INPUT-FLAG
variables.description: Overall input validation status flag for the current screen submission. Summarizes whether all fields entered by the administrator on the transaction type maintenance screen have passed validation, failed validation, or are awaiting initial entry.

variables.name: INPUT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that all administrator-entered fields on the transaction type maintenance screen have passed validation. When true, the workflow advances to the next step — either displaying the confirmation prompt or committing the database change.

variables.name: INPUT-ERROR
variables.description: Condition indicating that one or more fields entered by the administrator failed validation (e.g., blank transaction type code, invalid characters). When true, the screen is redisplayed with an error message identifying the problem so the administrator can correct it.

variables.name: INPUT-PENDING
variables.description: Condition indicating that no input validation has been performed yet for the current screen interaction — typically the initial state when the maintenance screen is first displayed and the administrator has not yet submitted any data.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-FLAG
variables.description: Controls whether the program should return control to the calling program (e.g., the transaction type list screen COTRTLIC or the admin menu COADM01C) rather than redisplaying the maintenance screen. Set when the administrator presses F3 to exit or completes a terminal action.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-FLAG-OFF
variables.description: Condition indicating that the program should continue processing and redisplay the transaction type maintenance screen — the normal state during an active add, update, or delete workflow.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-FLAG-ON
variables.description: Condition indicating that the program has finished its work and should transfer control back to the calling program — triggered when the administrator exits via F3 or when a terminal workflow step (such as a completed delete) has been reached.

variables.name: WS-PFK-FLAG
variables.description: Tracks whether the PF key pressed by the administrator is a recognized and permitted key for the current workflow step. Prevents the administrator from accidentally triggering unintended actions by pressing unsupported function keys on the transaction type maintenance screen.

variables.name: PFK-VALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator pressed a recognized PF key (e.g., Enter, F3, F4, F5, F12) that is valid for the current step of the transaction type maintenance workflow. Processing continues normally.

variables.name: PFK-INVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator pressed an unrecognized or unsupported PF key. When true, the program rejects the key press and displays an error message instructing the administrator to use only the permitted function keys for this screen.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-TTYP-FLAG
variables.description: Validation result flag specifically for the 2-character transaction type code field entered by the administrator. Indicates whether the code is valid, blank, or contains invalid characters — directly enforcing the business rule that transaction type codes must be non-blank and alphanumeric.

variables.name: FLG-TRANFILTER-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator-entered transaction type code has passed all validation checks — it is non-blank, exactly 2 characters, and alphanumeric. The workflow can proceed to the next step.

variables.name: FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator-entered transaction type code contains invalid characters. The screen is redisplayed with an error message requiring the administrator to enter a valid 2-character alphanumeric code.

variables.name: FLG-TRANFILTER-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator left the transaction type code field blank. Since a blank code is not a valid transaction type identifier, the program rejects the submission and prompts the administrator to enter a value.

variables.name: WS-NON-KEY-FLAGS
variables.description: Group of validation flags for non-key fields on the transaction type maintenance screen — specifically the transaction type description, which is a required but non-identifying field.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DESC-FLAGS
variables.description: Validation result flag for the transaction type description field entered by the administrator. Indicates whether the description is valid, blank, or otherwise unacceptable — enforcing the business rule that active transaction type records must have a non-blank description.

variables.name: FLG-DESCRIPTION-ISVALID
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator-entered transaction type description has passed validation — it is non-blank and within the 50-character limit. The workflow can proceed to the confirmation or commit step.

variables.name: FLG-DESCRIPTION-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator-entered transaction type description contains invalid content. The screen is redisplayed with an error message requiring the administrator to provide a valid description.

variables.name: FLG-DESCRIPTION-BLANK
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator left the transaction type description field blank. Since blank descriptions are not permitted for active transaction type records, the program rejects the submission and prompts the administrator to enter a description.

variables.name: CICS-OUTPUT-EDIT-VARS
variables.description: Group of formatting work areas used to prepare data for display on the transaction type maintenance screen — handles date formatting, currency display, and short alphanumeric/numeric output fields.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DATE-X
variables.description: Formatted date string (YYYY-MM-DD, 10 characters) used to display the current date on the transaction type maintenance screen header, giving the administrator a timestamp reference for the session.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Overlay structure that breaks the formatted date string into its individual year, month, and day components so each part can be populated or read separately when constructing the screen header date display.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DATE-X-YEAR
variables.description: 4-digit year portion of the current date displayed on the transaction type maintenance screen header (e.g., '2024').

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Separator character (typically a hyphen '-') between the year and month portions of the formatted date displayed on the screen header.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DATE-MONTH
variables.description: 2-digit month portion of the current date displayed on the transaction type maintenance screen header (e.g., '07' for July).

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Separator character (typically a hyphen '-') between the month and day portions of the formatted date displayed on the screen header.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DATE-DAY
variables.description: 2-digit day portion of the current date displayed on the transaction type maintenance screen header (e.g., '19' for the 19th).

variables.name: WS-EDIT-DATE-X
variables.description: Secondary overlay redefinition of the formatted date field — allows the date to be accessed or populated as an alternative layout, supporting flexible date formatting for the screen header display.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CURRENCY-9-2
variables.description: Character work area used as an intermediate buffer when formatting a currency amount for screen display — holds the raw numeric value before it is moved into the formatted currency display field.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-CURRENCY-9-2-F
variables.description: Formatted currency display field with sign, comma separators, and two decimal places. Used to present monetary amounts in a human-readable format on the screen — though primarily a general-purpose formatting variable, it may be used in the admin context for any monetary reference data displayed alongside transaction types.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-NUMERIC-2
variables.description: 2-digit numeric work area used for short numeric values during screen output formatting — a general-purpose field for holding small numeric codes or counts during display preparation.

variables.name: WS-EDIT-ALPHANUMERIC-2
variables.description: 2-character alphanumeric work area used during screen output formatting — well-suited for holding and displaying the 2-character transaction type code during screen preparation steps.

variables.name: WS-TABLE-READ-FLAGS
variables.description: Group of flags that record the outcome of reference table lookups performed during transaction type maintenance — used to determine whether a transaction type code was successfully found in the database.

variables.name: WS-TRANTYPE-MASTER-READ-FLAG
variables.description: Records whether the transaction type code entered by the administrator was found in the DCLTRTYP reference table. Drives the workflow decision of whether to proceed with an update/delete or to display a 'record not found' error message.

variables.name: FOUND-TRANTYPE-IN-TABLE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the transaction type code entered by the administrator exists in the DCLTRTYP reference table. When true, the program can proceed to display the record details and allow the administrator to update or delete it.

variables.name: TTYP-UPDATE-RECORD
variables.description: Working copy of the transaction type record being written to the DCLTRTYP database table during an add or update operation. Holds the final, validated values that will be committed to the database after the administrator confirms the change.

variables.name: TTUP-UPDATE-TTYP-TYPE
variables.description: The 2-character transaction type code that will be written to the DCLTRTYP database table during the commit step of an add or update operation. This is the administrator's confirmed new or corrected code, validated and ready for database storage.

variables.name: TTUP-UPDATE-TTYP-TYPE-DESC
variables.description: The up-to-50-character transaction type description that will be written to the DCLTRTYP database table during the commit step of an add or update operation. This is the administrator's confirmed new or corrected description, validated and ready for database storage.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Reserved padding space within a date/time working storage structure. Has no direct business meaning; it is a placeholder to align the date/time fields correctly in memory so the program can accurately display the current date and time on the transaction type maintenance screen.

variables.name: WS-INFO-MSG
variables.description: The instructional prompt message displayed on the Transaction Type maintenance screen to guide the bank administrator through the current step of the workflow. For example, it tells the administrator whether to enter a transaction type code to search, confirm a deletion, or press F5 to commit an update. This message changes at each stage of the add/update/delete process to keep the administrator informed of what action is expected next.

variables.name: WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE
variables.description: Condition indicating that no instructional prompt is currently needed on the screen. This occurs when the workflow is in a neutral state and no specific guidance needs to be shown to the administrator — for example, immediately after the screen is first displayed before any action has been taken.

variables.name: FOUND-TRANTYPE-DATA
variables.description: Condition indicating that the transaction type record was successfully retrieved from the database and its details are now displayed on screen. The administrator can see the current 2-character transaction type code and its description, and may proceed to update or delete the record.

variables.name: PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS
variables.description: Condition indicating that the screen is prompting the administrator to enter a transaction type code to search for an existing record. This is typically the initial state of the maintenance screen when no record has yet been looked up.

variables.name: PROMPT-CREATE-NEW-RECORD
variables.description: Condition indicating that the screen is prompting the administrator to enter the details for a brand-new transaction type record. This is shown when the administrator has chosen to add a new transaction type code and description that does not yet exist in the reference table.

variables.name: PROMPT-DELETE-CONFIRM
variables.description: Condition indicating that the screen is asking the administrator to explicitly confirm the deletion of the displayed transaction type record. This is the safety checkpoint before a transaction type code is permanently removed from the reference table, requiring the administrator to press F4 to proceed.

variables.name: CONFIRM-DELETE-SUCCESS
variables.description: Condition indicating that the transaction type record has been successfully deleted from the reference table. The screen displays this confirmation message so the administrator knows the removal was completed and the transaction type code is no longer active in the system.

variables.name: PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES
variables.description: Condition indicating that the screen is prompting the administrator to make changes to the currently displayed transaction type record. The record details are shown and the administrator is invited to modify the transaction type code or description fields before submitting the update.

variables.name: PROMPT-FOR-NEWDATA
variables.description: Condition indicating that the screen is prompting the administrator to enter new data values for the transaction type record being added or updated. This guides the administrator to fill in the required fields before the system can validate and process the change.

variables.name: PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION
variables.description: Condition indicating that the proposed changes to the transaction type record have been validated and are now displayed for the administrator's review. The administrator must press F5 to confirm and commit the update to the database, completing the mandatory two-step confirmation process for updates.

variables.name: CONFIRM-UPDATE-SUCCESS
variables.description: Condition indicating that the transaction type record has been successfully updated in the database. The screen displays this confirmation so the administrator knows the new transaction type code or description has been saved and is now active in the reference table.

variables.name: INFORM-FAILURE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the requested operation (add, update, or delete) has failed. The screen informs the administrator that the transaction type reference table could not be updated, prompting them to review the error details and take corrective action.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-MSG
variables.description: The error or status feedback message displayed on the Transaction Type maintenance screen after an action is attempted. This message tells the administrator the outcome of their last action — for example, that a record was not found, that a key was invalid, that the record was locked by another user, or that the update was cancelled. It is the primary communication channel for error handling and status reporting in the maintenance workflow.

variables.name: WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF
variables.description: Condition indicating that there is currently no error or status message to display to the administrator. The message area on the screen is blank, meaning the last operation completed without any issues requiring administrator attention.

variables.name: WS-EXIT-MESSAGE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator has chosen to exit the Transaction Type maintenance screen. The message confirms the exit action and signals that control is being returned to the administration menu (COADM01C), typically triggered by pressing F3.

variables.name: WS-INVALID-KEY
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator pressed a function key that is not valid or supported in the current context of the transaction type maintenance workflow. The administrator is notified so they can press a valid key to continue.

variables.name: WS-NAME-MUST-BE-ALPHA
variables.description: Condition indicating that the transaction type code or description entered by the administrator contains invalid characters. Per business rules, transaction type codes must be alphanumeric; this message rejects entries that do not meet that requirement and prompts the administrator to correct the input.

variables.name: WS-RECORD-NOT-FOUND
variables.description: Condition indicating that the transaction type code entered by the administrator does not exist in the Transaction Type reference table. The administrator is informed that no matching record was found, and they may need to verify the code or choose to create a new record.

variables.name: NO-SEARCH-CRITERIA-RECEIVED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator submitted the search form without entering a transaction type code. Since a 2-character code is required to look up a record, the system rejects the blank submission and prompts the administrator to provide a valid search key.

variables.name: NO-CHANGES-DETECTED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator submitted an update but the values entered are identical to what was originally retrieved from the database. Per business rules, the system detects this no-change situation and does not perform an unnecessary database write, informing the administrator that nothing was modified.

variables.name: COULD-NOT-LOCK-REC-FOR-UPDATE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the system was unable to obtain an exclusive lock on the transaction type record in the database in order to update it. This typically means another user or process is currently modifying the same record. The update is aborted and the administrator is notified to try again later.

variables.name: DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE
variables.description: Condition indicating that the transaction type record was modified by another user between the time the administrator fetched it for review and the time they attempted to commit their update. This concurrency protection prevents overwriting another user's changes; the administrator is warned and must re-fetch the record before retrying.

variables.name: WS-UPDATE-WAS-CANCELLED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator deliberately cancelled an in-progress update to the transaction type record, typically by pressing F12. No changes were saved to the database, and the system returns to a safe state with this cancellation confirmation message.

variables.name: TABLE-UPDATE-FAILED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the database update operation for the transaction type record failed unexpectedly. The transaction type reference table was not modified, and the administrator is notified of the failure so they can investigate or escalate the issue.

variables.name: RECORD-DELETE-FAILED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the attempt to delete the transaction type record from the reference table failed unexpectedly. The record remains in the database, and the administrator is informed of the failure so they can investigate the cause.

variables.name: WS-DELETE-WAS-CANCELLED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator deliberately cancelled an in-progress deletion of a transaction type record, typically by pressing F12 at the delete confirmation prompt. The record is preserved in the database, and the system confirms the cancellation to the administrator.

variables.name: WS-INVALID-KEY-PRESSED
variables.description: Condition indicating that the administrator pressed a function key that is not recognized or not applicable at the current step of the transaction type maintenance workflow. The system rejects the keypress and displays this message to guide the administrator to use a valid key.

variables.name: CODING-TO-BE-DONE
variables.description: Condition used as a development placeholder, indicating that a particular scenario or error path in the transaction type maintenance workflow has not yet been fully implemented. This would not appear in a production-ready system and signals incomplete business logic to developers.

variables.name: WS-LITERALS
variables.description: A group of constant reference values (literals) used throughout the Transaction Type maintenance program. These literals define the fixed identifiers for programs, transaction IDs, mapsets, and maps involved in the admin workflow, enabling consistent navigation between screens and programs without hardcoding values throughout the logic.

variables.name: LIT-THISPGM
variables.description: The CICS program name of this Transaction Type maintenance program itself (COTRTUPC). Used for self-identification in CICS communication areas and logging, ensuring the system knows which program is currently executing when passing control between programs.

variables.name: LIT-THISTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID associated with this Transaction Type maintenance program. Used to re-invoke this program after a screen interaction (pseudo-conversational return), ensuring the correct transaction is resumed when the administrator submits input on the maintenance screen.

variables.name: LIT-THISMAPSET
variables.description: The name of the BMS mapset (COTRTUP) that contains the screen layout for the Transaction Type maintenance screen. Used when sending or receiving the screen map to ensure the correct set of screen definitions is referenced.

variables.name: LIT-THISMAP
variables.description: The name of the specific BMS map within the COTRTUP mapset that defines the layout of the Transaction Type maintenance screen. Used in CICS SEND MAP and RECEIVE MAP commands to display and capture the administrator's input on the correct screen.

variables.name: LIT-ADMINPGM
variables.description: The CICS program name of the main administration menu program (COADM01C). Used when the administrator presses F3 to exit the Transaction Type maintenance screen and return to the top-level admin menu, enabling proper navigation back up the program hierarchy.

variables.name: LIT-ADMINTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID for the main administration menu program. Used when transferring control back to the admin menu so that CICS can correctly initiate the admin menu transaction when the administrator exits the Transaction Type maintenance screen.

variables.name: LIT-ADMINMAPSET
variables.description: The BMS mapset name for the main administration menu screen. Used when navigating back to the admin menu to ensure the correct screen layout is loaded for the administrator after exiting the Transaction Type maintenance program.

variables.name: LIT-ADMINMAP
variables.description: The specific BMS map name within the admin mapset that defines the administration menu screen layout. Used when returning control to the admin menu to display the correct menu screen to the administrator.

variables.name: LIT-LISTTPGM
variables.description: The CICS program name of the Transaction Type list/browse program (COTRTLIC) that called this maintenance program. Used to navigate back to the transaction type list screen, allowing the administrator to return to browsing the full list of transaction type codes after completing or cancelling a maintenance operation.

variables.name: LIT-LISTTTRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction ID for the Transaction Type list/browse program. Used when transferring control back to the list screen so CICS can correctly initiate the list transaction, enabling the administrator to resume browsing transaction type records.

variables.name: LIT-LISTTMAPSET
variables.description: The BMS mapset name for the Transaction Type list/browse screen. Used when navigating back to the list screen to ensure the correct screen layout is loaded for the administrator to view the list of transaction type codes.

variables.name: LIT-LISTTMAP
variables.description: The specific BMS map name within the list mapset that defines the Transaction Type list/browse screen layout. Used when returning to the list screen to display the correct browsing interface to the administrator.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-ALPHANUM-FROM-X
variables.description: A group containing the complete set of valid alphanumeric characters (uppercase letters, lowercase letters, and digits 0–9) used as the source reference for input validation. This enables the program to verify that transaction type codes entered by the administrator contain only permitted characters, enforcing the business rule that codes must be alphanumeric.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM-X
variables.description: A sub-group containing all valid alphabetic characters (uppercase and lowercase letters) used as a reference for alphabetic input validation. Supports checking whether administrator-entered values contain only letters when alphabetic-only fields are required.

variables.name: LIT-UPPER
variables.description: A string containing all 26 uppercase letters of the alphabet (A–Z). Used as the source reference in character translation or validation routines to verify that transaction type codes or descriptions contain valid uppercase alphabetic characters.

variables.name: LIT-LOWER
variables.description: A string containing all 26 lowercase letters of the alphabet (a–z). Used alongside LIT-UPPER in character validation routines to accept or translate lowercase alphabetic input from the administrator when validating transaction type data.

variables.name: LIT-NUMBERS
variables.description: A string containing all 10 numeric digit characters (0–9). Used in input validation to verify that transaction type codes contain only permitted numeric characters, supporting the business rule that codes must be alphanumeric.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM
variables.description: A 52-character working copy of all valid alphabetic characters (both upper and lower case combined), initialized to spaces and populated at runtime for use as the source argument in INSPECT or string translation statements when validating that administrator input contains only alphabetic characters.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-ALPHANUM-FROM
variables.description: A 62-character working copy of all valid alphanumeric characters (letters and digits combined), initialized to spaces and populated at runtime for use as the source argument in character validation routines to enforce the business rule that transaction type codes must be alphanumeric.

variables.name: LIT-ALL-NUM-FROM
variables.description: A 10-character working copy of all valid numeric digit characters (0–9), initialized to spaces and populated at runtime for use as the source argument in numeric character validation routines when checking administrator-entered values.

variables.name: LIT-ALPHA-SPACES-TO
variables.description: A 52-character target field filled with spaces, used as the destination argument paired with LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM in INSPECT CONVERTING statements. This allows the program to blank out or detect non-alphabetic characters in administrator input during validation of transaction type fields.

variables.name: LIT-ALPHANUM-SPACES-TO
variables.description: A 62-character target field filled with spaces, used as the destination argument paired with LIT-ALL-ALPHANUM-FROM in INSPECT CONVERTING statements. This enables the program to identify and handle non-alphanumeric characters in administrator input, enforcing the business rule that transaction type codes must be alphanumeric.

variables.name: LIT-NUM-SPACES-TO
variables.description: A 10-character target field filled with spaces, used as the destination argument paired with LIT-ALL-NUM-FROM in INSPECT CONVERTING statements. This allows the program to detect non-numeric characters in fields that require numeric-only input during transaction type data validation.

variables.name: WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA
variables.description: The CICS communication area (COMMAREA) structure for this Transaction Type maintenance program. This is the data container passed between CICS pseudo-conversational invocations of the program, preserving the administrator's current workflow state, the data being maintained, and the stage of the add/update/delete process across multiple screen interactions.

variables.name: TTUP-UPDATE-SCREEN-DATA
variables.description: The section of the COMMAREA that holds all data related to the current transaction type maintenance session on screen. This group preserves the administrator's in-progress work — including the action being performed, the original record values, and the new values entered — across the pseudo-conversational CICS interactions required to complete an add, update, or delete operation.

variables.name: TTUP-CHANGE-ACTION
variables.description: A single-character state machine flag that tracks which stage of the transaction type maintenance workflow the administrator is currently in. It controls the program's behavior on each screen interaction — for example, whether to fetch a record, display it for review, await update confirmation, or confirm a deletion. Valid states include S (show details), N (changes validated, awaiting confirmation), C (changes committed), 9 (confirm delete), and 7 (delete completed).

variables.name: TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED
variables.description: Condition indicating that no transaction type record has yet been retrieved from the database for this session. This is the initial state when the maintenance screen is first entered, before the administrator has searched for or selected a transaction type code to work with.

variables.name: TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS
variables.description: Condition (state = 'K') indicating that the administrator submitted a search with invalid or missing transaction type code input. The program has detected that the search criteria do not meet the business rules (e.g., blank or non-alphanumeric code) and is waiting for the administrator to provide a valid 2-character transaction type code.

variables.name: TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND
variables.description: Condition (state = 'X') indicating that the transaction type code entered by the administrator was searched in the database but no matching record exists in the Transaction Type reference table. The administrator is informed that the record was not found and may choose to create a new one or search again.

variables.name: TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS
variables.description: Condition (state = 'S') indicating that a transaction type record has been successfully retrieved from the database and its details — the 2-character code and 50-character description — are currently displayed on the maintenance screen for the administrator to review, update, or delete.

variables.name: TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD
variables.description: Condition flag indicating the administrator is in the process of creating a brand-new transaction type record that does not yet exist in the database. When true, the workflow is in 'new record entry' mode.

variables.name: TTUP-REVIEW-NEW-RECORD
variables.description: Condition flag indicating the administrator is reviewing a newly entered transaction type record before it is saved. This represents the preview/review step in the add-new-record workflow, where the administrator can verify the data before committing.

variables.name: TTUP-DELETE-IN-PROGRESS
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that a deletion of a transaction type record is currently underway and awaiting administrator confirmation. This guards against accidental deletion by requiring an explicit confirmation step before the record is permanently removed.

variables.name: TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE
variables.description: Condition flag (sharing value '9' with TTUP-DELETE-IN-PROGRESS) indicating the system is waiting for the administrator to explicitly press F4 to confirm the deletion of the transaction type record. This is the mandatory confirmation gate before any record is permanently deleted.

variables.name: TTUP-START-DELETE
variables.description: Condition flag indicating the administrator has initiated a delete request for a transaction type record. This is the first step of the deletion workflow — the record has been identified for deletion but the confirmation prompt has not yet been presented to the administrator.

variables.name: TTUP-DELETE-DONE
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the deletion of the transaction type record has been successfully completed. The record has been permanently removed from the Transaction Type reference table and the administrator can be notified of the successful deletion.

variables.name: TTUP-DELETE-FAILED
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the attempted deletion of the transaction type record failed — for example, due to a database error or a locking conflict. The administrator must be notified that the record was NOT removed and the deletion did not succeed.

variables.name: TTUP-CHANGES-MADE
variables.description: Condition flag indicating the administrator has entered changes to the transaction type record (either with validation errors still present, or with valid changes awaiting confirmation). Used broadly to detect that the workflow is in an active edit state, regardless of whether the changes have passed validation.

variables.name: TTUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK
variables.description: Condition flag indicating the administrator has submitted changes to the transaction type record, but those changes failed validation (e.g., blank transaction type code, invalid characters, or blank description). The administrator must correct the errors before proceeding.

variables.name: TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED
variables.description: Condition flag indicating the administrator's changes to the transaction type record have passed all validation checks and are displayed for review, but the administrator has not yet pressed F5 to confirm and commit the update to the database. This is the mandatory review step before any changes are saved.

variables.name: TTUP-CHANGES-FAILED
variables.description: Condition flag indicating that the confirmed update to the transaction type record failed during the database write operation — either because the record could not be locked (another user has it), or because the actual database update itself failed. The administrator must be notified that the changes were NOT saved.

variables.name: TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR
variables.description: Condition flag indicating the administrator confirmed the update, but the system could not obtain an exclusive lock on the transaction type record in the database — meaning another user or process is currently modifying it. The update is aborted and the administrator is notified to try again later.

variables.name: TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED
variables.description: Condition flag indicating the administrator confirmed the update and the record was locked successfully, but the actual database write (UPDATE SQL) failed for another reason (e.g., concurrent modification detected, DB2 error). The changes were not committed and the administrator must be informed of the failure.

variables.name: TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE
variables.description: Condition flag indicating the administrator's changes to the transaction type record have been successfully validated, confirmed, and committed to the database. The transaction type code and/or description have been permanently updated in the reference table.

variables.name: TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT
variables.description: Condition flag indicating the administrator cancelled an in-progress update or delete operation, and the system has safely returned to a neutral state without making any changes to the transaction type reference data. This confirms a clean cancellation with no partial updates.

variables.name: TTUP-OLD-DETAILS
variables.description: Group record holding the original transaction type data as it was retrieved from the database before the administrator made any changes. Used to detect concurrent modifications by another user and to determine whether the administrator has actually changed anything.

variables.name: TTUP-OLD-TTYP-DATA
variables.description: Sub-group containing the original transaction type code and description as fetched from the Transaction Type reference table. Serves as the baseline snapshot for change detection and concurrency checking during the update workflow.

variables.name: TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE
variables.description: The original 2-character transaction type code (e.g., 'PU' for Purchase, 'RF' for Refund) as it was read from the database before the administrator began editing. Used to detect if another user has changed the record between the time it was fetched and the time the update is submitted, preventing overwriting of concurrent changes.

variables.name: TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC
variables.description: The original 50-character description of the transaction type (e.g., 'Purchase at point of sale') as it was read from the database before editing began. Used alongside the original code to detect concurrent modifications by another administrator and to determine whether the current administrator has actually changed the description.

variables.name: TTUP-NEW-DETAILS
variables.description: Group record holding the new transaction type data as entered by the administrator on the maintenance screen. These are the proposed changes that will be validated and, upon confirmation, written to the Transaction Type reference table.

variables.name: TTUP-NEW-TTYP-DATA
variables.description: Sub-group containing the new transaction type code and description as entered by the administrator. These values are subject to validation rules (non-blank, alphanumeric code, non-blank description) before being eligible for confirmation and database commit.

variables.name: TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE
variables.description: The new 2-character transaction type code entered by the administrator on the maintenance screen (e.g., changing 'PU' to 'PS'). This value is validated to be non-blank and alphanumeric before the update can proceed. For new records, this becomes the primary key of the new Transaction Type reference entry.

variables.name: TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC
variables.description: The new 50-character transaction type description entered by the administrator on the maintenance screen (e.g., 'Point of Sale Purchase'). This value must not be blank; it is validated before the update is allowed to proceed and becomes the human-readable label for the transaction type in the reference table.

variables.name: WS-COMMAREA
variables.description: Working storage area used to hold the full communication area (COMMAREA) data passed between CICS programs. This 2000-byte buffer preserves the administrator's session context — including workflow state, original record values, and navigation information — across multiple screen interactions and program transfers within the CardDemo admin workflow.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The standard CICS communication area passed into this program when it is invoked. Contains the session state and context data (workflow flags, original record values, navigation pointers) passed from the previous program in the admin workflow (e.g., COTRTLIC list screen), enabling the program to resume the correct step of the transaction type maintenance process.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Unused padding byte at the start of the CICS COMMAREA structure. Has no direct business meaning; it is a structural placeholder to align the COMMAREA layout with the expected data format passed between programs in the CardDemo admin workflow.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
paragraphs.description: This is the main orchestration entry point for the Transaction Type maintenance screen. It initialises the session, determines the administrator's intent based on their PF key and workflow state, and routes control to the appropriate processing step — whether that is displaying the screen, validating input, confirming a change, saving an update, or executing a deletion.

paragraphs.name: COMMON-RETURN
paragraphs.description: Finalises the current interaction cycle by packaging any error or status message along with the full session context, then suspends the program and hands control back to the CICS transaction manager, ready to resume when the administrator next interacts with the screen.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal exit point of the main transaction processing routine for the Transaction Type maintenance screen. This is a structural boundary that ensures control returns cleanly to the CICS transaction manager after all screen interaction, validation, and database operations have been completed.

paragraphs.name: 0001-CHECK-PFKEYS
paragraphs.description: Validates whether the PF key pressed by the administrator is permitted given the current stage of the transaction type maintenance workflow. Keys that are not applicable to the current workflow state are rejected, and an error message is queued to guide the administrator.

paragraphs.name: 0001-CHECK-PFKEYS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This is the exit point paragraph that marks the end of the PF key validation routine. It serves as a structured termination label allowing the program to cleanly return control to the calling paragraph after all PF key checks and workflow routing decisions have been completed.

paragraphs.name: 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS
paragraphs.description: Orchestrates the full input processing cycle for the Transaction Type maintenance screen: captures what the administrator entered, stores the new values, validates them for business rule compliance, and prepares the screen state for the next interaction step.

paragraphs.name: 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal exit point of the input processing routine, allowing the workflow engine to cleanly return control after all administrator inputs, PF key actions, and screen validations have been evaluated.

paragraphs.name: 1100-RECEIVE-MAP
paragraphs.description: Captures the administrator's input from the Transaction Type maintenance screen, collecting any entered transaction type codes, descriptions, and PF key selections submitted by the administrator for processing.

paragraphs.name: 1100-RECEIVE-MAP-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the map-receive routine, marking the end of the screen input capture phase before the program proceeds to process the administrator's entered data and PF key selections.

paragraphs.name: 1150-STORE-MAP-IN-NEW
paragraphs.description: Captures and validates the administrator's screen input for transaction type code and description, storing the entered values as the new candidate data for the add/update operation. Blank or placeholder entries are treated as absent, while valid entries are trimmed and recorded for subsequent workflow processing.

paragraphs.name: 1150-STORE-MAP-IN-NEW-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This is a terminal exit point for the paragraph that captures and stores the administrator's newly entered transaction type data from the screen. It serves as a structural boundary marker in the workflow, signalling the completion of the data-capture phase before processing continues.

paragraphs.name: 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS
paragraphs.description: Validates all administrator inputs on the Transaction Type maintenance screen before any database operation is attempted. It enforces business rules around the transaction type code and description, detects no-change scenarios, and advances the workflow state to 'awaiting confirmation' when all inputs are valid.

paragraphs.name: 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the input validation routine (1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS), marking the end of all administrator input checks for transaction type code and description before the workflow proceeds to the next step.

paragraphs.name: 1205-COMPARE-OLD-NEW
paragraphs.description: Determines whether the administrator has actually made any changes to the transaction type record by comparing the newly entered code and description against the original values retrieved from the database. This enforces the business rule that a confirmation workflow is only triggered when real modifications exist, preventing unnecessary update operations.

paragraphs.name: 1205-COMPARE-OLD-NEW-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the old-versus-new value comparison routine, which detects whether the administrator has actually changed any transaction type fields compared to what was originally retrieved from the database.

paragraphs.name: 1210-EDIT-TRANTYPE
paragraphs.description: Validates the transaction type code entered by the administrator, ensuring it is a non-blank, 2-character alphanumeric value, then normalises it to a zero-padded numeric format so it is stored consistently in the database.

paragraphs.name: 1210-EDIT-TRANTYPE-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point of the transaction type editing and validation routine (1210-EDIT-TRANTYPE), allowing control to return to the calling workflow step after all input validation checks on the transaction type code and description have been completed.

paragraphs.name: 1230-EDIT-ALPHANUM-REQD
paragraphs.description: Validates that a required alphanumeric field (such as a transaction type code or description) has been supplied by the administrator and contains only letters, numbers, or spaces — rejecting blank entries and entries with special characters before they can be saved to the database.

paragraphs.name: 1230-EDIT-ALPHANUM-REQD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the exit point for the alphanumeric field validation routine, marking the end of the required-field format check used to enforce that transaction type codes and descriptions contain valid, non-blank alphanumeric content before any database operation proceeds.

paragraphs.name: 1245-EDIT-NUM-REQD
paragraphs.description: Validates that a required numeric field entered by the administrator is present, contains only numeric digits, and is not zero. Used to enforce data integrity rules on mandatory numeric inputs before any database operation is attempted.

paragraphs.name: 1245-EDIT-NUM-REQD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This is a structural exit point paragraph that marks the end of the numeric field validation routine (1245-EDIT-NUM-REQD). It serves as the return boundary after the program has finished checking whether a required numeric field contains a valid value.

paragraphs.name: 2000-DECIDE-ACTION
paragraphs.description: Routes the administrator's current action to the correct workflow stage based on the combination of the screen's current state and the PF key pressed, acting as the central decision engine that advances, cancels, or holds the transaction type maintenance workflow.

paragraphs.name: 2000-DECIDE-ACTION-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the action-decision routing logic, marking the end of the workflow stage determination process that directs the administrator's request to the appropriate add, update, or delete handling routine.

paragraphs.name: 3000-SEND-MAP
paragraphs.description: Orchestrates the full preparation and delivery of the Transaction Type maintenance screen to the bank administrator, coordinating all steps from initialising the screen layout, populating current data values, setting contextual guidance messages, applying field-level visual attributes, and finally transmitting the completed screen to the administrator's terminal.

paragraphs.name: 3000-SEND-MAP-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the end of the screen-sending routine (3000-SEND-MAP), serving as a structured exit point that returns control to the calling workflow step after the Transaction Type maintenance screen has been presented to the administrator.

paragraphs.name: 3100-SCREEN-INIT
paragraphs.description: Initialises the Transaction Type maintenance screen with standard header information — application titles, program identity, and the current date and time — so the administrator sees a properly branded, timestamped workspace before any data entry or record lookup begins.

paragraphs.name: 3100-SCREEN-INIT-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal end boundary of the screen initialisation routine, serving as the structured exit point that returns control to the calling workflow step after the screen setup is complete.

paragraphs.name: 3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS
paragraphs.description: Determines what data to display on the Transaction Type maintenance screen based on the current stage of the administrator's workflow, ensuring the screen always reflects the correct values (initial, original, or updated) for the step the administrator is at.

paragraphs.name: 3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the screen variable setup routine (3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS), marking the end of the process that prepares all display fields, messages, and workflow state indicators before presenting the Transaction Type maintenance screen to the administrator.

paragraphs.name: 3201-SHOW-INITIAL-VALUES
paragraphs.description: Clears the transaction type code field on the maintenance screen to present a blank, ready-to-use input area when the administrator first accesses the update screen. This ensures no stale or residual data is displayed before the administrator enters or retrieves a transaction type record.

paragraphs.name: 3201-SHOW-INITIAL-VALUES-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This is the formal exit point of the 3201-SHOW-INITIAL-VALUES routine, which is responsible for populating the maintenance screen with the current transaction type data retrieved from the database. It marks the boundary of that display-preparation logic, returning control to the calling workflow step.

paragraphs.name: 3202-SHOW-ORIGINAL-VALUES
paragraphs.description: Prepares the maintenance screen to display the original, unmodified transaction type record retrieved from the database, allowing the administrator to review the current values before deciding whether to make changes.

paragraphs.name: 3202-SHOW-ORIGINAL-VALUES-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal exit point of the routine that displays the original transaction type record values to the administrator. This is a standard structured programming terminator for the 3202-SHOW-ORIGINAL-VALUES paragraph, ensuring clean control flow back to the calling workflow step.

paragraphs.name: 3203-SHOW-UPDATED-VALUES
paragraphs.description: Refreshes the maintenance screen with the administrator's newly entered transaction type code and description, so they can review the pending changes before confirming or cancelling the update.

paragraphs.name: 3203-SHOW-UPDATED-VALUES-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal end of the 'Show Updated Values' routine, which presents the administrator with the validated transaction type changes awaiting confirmation. This is a standard structural exit point that returns control to the calling workflow step.

paragraphs.name: 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG
paragraphs.description: Determines the appropriate guidance message to display to the administrator based on the current stage of the transaction type maintenance workflow, then formats and renders that message — along with any error status — on the maintenance screen.

paragraphs.name: 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the informational message setup routine (3250-SETUP-INFOMSG), which prepares the on-screen guidance messages that direct the administrator through the current step of the update/delete workflow. It contains no logic itself, acting purely as a structured termination marker for the paragraph.

paragraphs.name: 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS
paragraphs.description: Configures the screen's field protection, cursor positioning, and color highlighting based on the current workflow stage, ensuring administrators can only edit fields appropriate to their current step (search, edit, confirm, or delete) and receive clear visual feedback about errors or required actions.

paragraphs.name: 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This is the exit point (terminator) of the screen attribute setup routine. It marks the end of the paragraph that configures the visual presentation of the Transaction Type maintenance screen, allowing control to return to the calling workflow step.

paragraphs.name: 3310-PROTECT-ALL-ATTRS
paragraphs.description: Locks all interactive fields on the Transaction Type maintenance screen to prevent the administrator from modifying them during a workflow step that requires read-only display, such as the confirmation or delete confirmation stage.

paragraphs.name: 3310-PROTECT-ALL-ATTRS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This is the exit point of the 'protect all screen attributes' routine, marking the end of the paragraph that locks all input fields on the maintenance screen to prevent administrator edits during read-only or confirmation display states.

paragraphs.name: 3320-UNPROTECT-FEW-ATTRS
paragraphs.description: Configures the screen field attributes to allow the administrator to edit the transaction type description field, while making the informational prompt message read-only so it cannot be accidentally overwritten during the update workflow.

paragraphs.name: 3320-UNPROTECT-FEW-ATTRS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This is the exit point (terminator) of the paragraph that controls which screen fields are made editable during the update/maintenance workflow. It marks the end of the field-protection logic and returns control to the calling routine.

paragraphs.name: 3390-SETUP-INFOMSG-ATTRS
paragraphs.description: Controls the visual prominence of the informational guidance message on the maintenance screen: if there is no current guidance message to show, the message field is dimmed/hidden; otherwise it is highlighted to draw the administrator's attention to the next required action in the workflow.

paragraphs.name: 3390-SETUP-INFOMSG-ATTRS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This is the exit point (terminator) of the paragraph responsible for configuring informational message display attributes on the administrator's screen. It marks the end of the screen guidance message setup routine, returning control to the calling workflow step.

paragraphs.name: 3391-SETUP-PFKEY-ATTRS
paragraphs.description: Configures which PF key options are visually available to the administrator on the maintenance screen based on the current workflow stage, ensuring only contextually valid actions are presented at each step of the add/update/delete process.

paragraphs.name: 3391-SETUP-PFKEY-ATTRS-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This is the exit point (terminator) of the PF key attribute setup routine. It marks the end of the paragraph that configures screen field attributes based on the current workflow state, allowing control to return to the calling paragraph.

paragraphs.name: 3400-SEND-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Renders and displays the Transaction Type maintenance screen to the bank administrator, presenting the current state of the workflow (data entry, confirmation prompt, or error message) and positioning the cursor for the next required input.

paragraphs.name: 3400-SEND-SCREEN-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal end of the screen-sending routine, serving as a structured exit point that returns control to the calling workflow step after the Transaction Type maintenance screen has been presented to the administrator.

paragraphs.name: 9000-READ-TRANTYPE
paragraphs.description: Retrieves a transaction type record from the database by its 2-character code, validates that the lookup was successful, and preserves the original field values to enable later concurrency detection and change comparison during the update workflow.

paragraphs.name: 9000-READ-TRANTYPE-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal exit point of the transaction type record retrieval routine, allowing the program to return control to the calling workflow step after the database lookup has completed.

paragraphs.name: 9100-GET-TRANSACTION-TYPE
paragraphs.description: Looks up a transaction type record in the database using the 2-character code entered by the administrator, confirming whether the code exists and retrieving its current description for display or further processing.

paragraphs.name: 9100-GET-TRANSACTION-TYPE-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the transaction type retrieval routine, marking the end of the database lookup process that fetches a transaction type record for display or maintenance by the administrator.

paragraphs.name: 9500-STORE-FETCHED-DATA
paragraphs.description: Captures a snapshot of the transaction type record as it was originally retrieved from the database, preserving the original code and description so the program can later detect if another user has modified the record before the administrator's changes are committed.

paragraphs.name: 9500-STORE-FETCHED-DATA-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the end of the routine that saves the originally retrieved transaction type record data (code and description) into working storage for later use in concurrency checking and change detection. This is a structural exit point with no additional business logic of its own.

paragraphs.name: 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING
paragraphs.description: Commits the administrator's approved transaction type description change to the database, then evaluates the outcome to determine the next workflow state — whether the update succeeded, the record needs to be inserted as new, a locking conflict occurred, or a database error was encountered.

paragraphs.name: 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal end of the write processing routine for transaction type records. This is a structural exit point that allows the database write workflow to return control cleanly to the calling logic after a create, update, or delete operation has been completed.

paragraphs.name: 9700-INSERT-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Permanently creates a new Transaction Type reference record in the database with the administrator-supplied code and description. If the insert succeeds, the change is committed as a durable transaction; if it fails, the operation is aborted and the administrator is notified with a diagnostic error message.

paragraphs.name: 9700-INSERT-RECORD-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal exit point for the new transaction type record insertion routine. It marks the end of the insert workflow step, returning control to the calling logic after a new transaction type has been added to the database.

paragraphs.name: 9800-DELETE-PROCESSING
paragraphs.description: Executes the permanent removal of a confirmed transaction type record from the reference database, then evaluates the outcome to either commit the deletion or inform the administrator of the specific reason for failure, including referential integrity violations.

paragraphs.name: 9800-DELETE-PROCESSING-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph marks the formal exit point of the delete processing workflow, and is immediately followed by shared utility code that captures and stores which PF key the administrator pressed, enabling the program to correctly interpret the administrator's next intended action (confirm deletion, cancel, navigate, etc.).

paragraphs.name: ABEND-ROUTINE
paragraphs.description: Handles unrecoverable system failures in the Transaction Type maintenance program by capturing diagnostic information, notifying the administrator's screen, and forcing a controlled CICS transaction termination to prevent data corruption or silent failures.

paragraphs.name: ABEND-ROUTINE-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Marks the formal end of the abnormal termination handling routine for the Transaction Type maintenance program. This exit point ensures the ABEND-ROUTINE paragraph has a clean structural boundary, allowing COBOL flow control to return correctly after any critical error handling has completed.
